methods.deseasonalisation: Each calendar month's mean over the selected period is subtracted (anomalies).
methods.trend: Ordinary least squares slope of the anomalies, reported per decade.
methods.uncertainty: Two memory corrections: month to month (AR(1) for the actual sampling, bias-corrected; Santer et al. 2000) and year to year (the same test on yearly means). The p-value is the larger of the two and the 95% interval covers both, so a trend counts only if both agree.
methods.cross_check: Seasonal Mann–Kendall with the Hirsch & Slack (1984) correction for dependent months, and Mann–Kendall on yearly means with the Hamed & Rao (1998) correction; the larger p is shown. Seasonal Sen slope.
methods.calibration: Checked on synthetic series without a trend: with month-to-month memory up to 0.9, seasons and gaps, at most about 6% are called significant (the target is 5%). Slow decade-long swings remain hard: 5–12% instead of 12–39% before this correction.
methods.map_multiple_testing: Benjamini–Hochberg false discovery rate across map cells, q = 0.05 (Wilks 2016).
methods.period_choice: The map correction covers grid cells, not the choice of period, season or variable: the more combinations you try, the more likely one looks significant by chance. The squares in “Does it hold?” overlap, so they are not independent repeats.
methods.regional_mean: cos(latitude)-weighted mean of cell anomalies; months with < 50% area coverage are dropped.
methods.minimum_data: A trend is computed only if at least 70% of the selected months are valid.
